content: Each uploaded file is associated with an image page. This page serves as an image description page, providing detailed information about the image. If a family of projects has a Commons project, the file is typically uploaded to Commons. The image page on Commons includes copyright information. In the internal image syntax, the filename is assumed to refer to the file within the same project if it exists there; otherwise, it refers to the file on Commons. When naming a file on Commons, avoid using a name already in use on any project where the file may be utilized unless the new file is intended to replace the local one (which will then be deleted) or unless the Commons image is to be replaced locally with a local version without altering the links. An image on Commons can have a separate image page on every project that does not already have another image with the same name. If the projects are distinguished by language, the local image page can provide information about the image in the local language. This also allows for categorizing the image within the local category system and shows the local pages that use the image. To determine which pages of which projects use an image on Commons, it is essential to link the image page on Commons to all local image pages of that image. Even if the local image page has never been explicitly created and is therefore empty, a link to the page generates a section called image links, showing the local pages that use the image. The interlanguage link feature works on Commons and produces links to the Wikipedias. Links to other projects are displayed in-page. The image is linked to the local image description page, which, due to the contents of MediaWiki:Sharedupload, is linked to the one on Commons where the image was uploaded. To create a link to the image description page of a sound file or an image without embedding the actual image, use a link like `[[:File:Example.jpg]]`. For images, the leading colon prevents the image from being embedded in the article and instead creates a standard link. For sound files, automatic playback is not possible anyway. The description page consists of four parts: 1. The image itself (in the case of an image). 2. A description of the image or sound. 3. The Image history, which refers to the page history. 4. The Image links or File links section, which lists pages embedding the image or linking to it with Media:. However, it does not list links to the image page for an image in a template; it only lists the template, not the pages where the template is used. If an image in a template depends on a parameter with the entire image code, the URL of the image, or variables like `{{PAGENAME}}`, it does not show the final page or the template. If only the caption is a parameter, the template is listed. The description part also has an edit history, labeled Image: xxx Revision history, which should not be confused with the Image history. This section primarily refers to the description part and is particularly relevant for images. For sound files, additional information can be found on Wikipedia's media guidelines. Useful Information to Include on an Image Description Page In the description section of the page, you can include text. Initially, this section automatically contains the upload summary provided by the user when uploading the first version of the file. This text also appears in the Image history section at the first upload line. Description of the Image For example: Image of a goldfish in a small tank. This should not serve as alternative text but rather as a description. This is useful for users who do not have direct access to the image and acts as a temporary substitute for a proper long description tag. You can also include the dimensions of the image in pixels. Other Versions If other versions of the same image exist (especially larger versions), link to them. Text-free versions are particularly useful for use across different language versions. Categorizing Images Images can belong to the same category as other pages but are treated separately. On the category page, they are not included in the count of articles in the category and are displayed in a separate section with a thumbnail and the name of each image. On Commons, there are essentially only images. On projects with real articles, a category can either mix articles and images about a subject or have separate image categories. An image category is typically a subcategory of the general category about the same subject and a subcategory of a broader image category. To categorize a new image, the image page does not need to be edited. The category tag can simply be added in the upload summary. Many images can be categorized in one of the subcategories of Category: Images by subject. You may need to explore the category hierarchy to find the appropriate place. Editing The preview of the edit page for an image page only shows the editable part, not the image itself, the image history, or the image links. Through this edit page, the image file itself cannot be edited. Uploading a new image file requires a new upload. A new image under the name of an existing image can only be uploaded by a system operator (sysop).
